title: Daily Market Digest: October 23, 2026
subtitle: Market sentiment weighed by tech sell-off, rising oil prices

items.headline: U.S. Stocks Slide Amid Tech Sell-Off and Surging Oil Prices
items.summary: U.S. equities are predominantly lower today, continuing a trend from Thursday's session, as investor concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) spending sustainability and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, pushing crude oil prices higher, dampen market sentiment. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq are recording declines, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average is also down, indicating broad-market pressure.

items.statContext: Down 0.5% today. The index fell 1.2% to 7,663.43 on Thursday, marking its worst day since July.
Down 0.1% today. The tech-heavy index plunged 2.6% or 694 points to 26,008.86 on Thursday.
Down 1.1% today. The Dow posted a marginal gain of 11.89 points to close at 52,867.98 on Thursday.

items.headline: Spotify Surges on Strong Q4 Outlook
items.summary: Spotify shares rose after the music streaming firm forecast fourth-quarter profit above Wall Street estimates, buoyed by its AI-powered features designed to drive user growth.

items.headline: Procter & Gamble Jumps After Earnings Beat
items.summary: Procter & Gamble saw its stock climb to a near eight-month high after the consumer goods giant surpassed first-quarter earnings estimates.

items.headline: Micron Technology Posts Solid Gains
items.summary: Micron Technology shares recorded notable gains today, helping to offset some of the broader market pressure.

items.headline: American Express Falls on Workforce Reduction Plans
items.summary: American Express shares declined after the credit card giant's CEO announced plans to eliminate approximately 5% of its global workforce, incurring a $336 million restructuring charge in the third quarter.

items.headline: Sallie Mae Tumbles on Q3 Loss and Weak Guidance
items.summary: SLM Corp., known as Sallie Mae, experienced a significant drop in its stock price after reporting a third-quarter loss of 19 cents per share, contrary to analyst expectations for a profit, and providing full-year guidance significantly below consensus.

items.headline: Kinsale Capital Group Down Despite Earnings Beat
items.summary: Kinsale Capital Group shares fell despite the specialty property and casualty insurer beating third-quarter earnings estimates, as news of its CFO's upcoming retirement weighed on investor sentiment.

items.headline: Technology Sector Leads Market Decline; Consumer Staples Show Resilience
items.summary: The technology sector, particularly AI-related stocks and semiconductors, continued to be a significant drag on the broader market, extending Thursday's sharp sell-off. Concerns over capital expenditure for AI infrastructure and its sustainability are driving the weakness. In contrast, defensive sectors like Consumer Staples demonstrated resilience, with some stocks posting notable gains.

items.headline: PMI and Consumer Sentiment Data Released; Fed in Blackout Period
items.summary: Today's economic calendar included the release of October's flash S&P Global Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) readings for manufacturing and services, alongside the final University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment survey. The Federal Reserve remains in its blackout period ahead of its October 27-28 FOMC meeting next week, where interest rates are widely expected to remain unchanged.

items.headline: Major Earnings Reports Highlight AI Investment Concerns
items.summary: Earnings reports from major companies continue to influence market movements. While Meta Platforms and Tesla delivered results earlier this week, their capital expenditure guidance for AI initiatives stoked fears that the AI investment boom might be peaking, contributing to the tech sell-off. Today, American Express reported mixed Q3 results and announced a workforce reduction, while Balchem Corporation posted healthy growth across all segments for Q3 2026.

items.headline: Oil Prices Surge Amid Middle East Tensions; Treasury Yields Fluctuate
items.summary: Crude oil prices surged, with Brent crude trading above $116 per barrel, fueled by rising geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and concerns over global energy supply. In the bond market, the yield on the 10-year Treasury note, which saw a significant drop on Thursday, edged higher today to 5.00%.
